TENTATIVE RULING

Case: Machorro – Trust 01389717
Date: March 13, 2026

MOTION TO COMPEL RESPONSES TO FORM INTERROGATORIES (ROA 223)

Petitioner Vanessa Stone (“Petitioner”) moves to compel initial responses to form interrogatories from Respondent Lorelei Ann Griggs (“Respondent”). Petitioner further moves for monetary sanctions in the amount of $1,060.00.

In opposition, Respondent states that she served initial responses on November 7, 2025, and supplemental responses on December 22, 2025.

In reply, Petitioner states that the untimely responses served on November 7, 2025, were “deficient and failed to comply with the discovery laws.” The alleged deficiencies were not specified, and a copy of the responses was not provided to the court. Moreover, Petitioner does not mention the supplemental responses served on December 22, 2025. Thus, the court is unable to issue any orders regarding the substance of the discovery responses.

Since responses to the form interrogatories have been served, the motion to compel responses is DENIED as moot.
Respondent argues that the imposition of sanctions would be unjust because
her delay in responding to discovery was caused by several factors.
First, Respondent claims that, for unexplained reasons, any mail sent to her
house does not reach her directly. The court finds such argument unpersuasive.
The discovery was properly served by mail to Respondent’s designated address
for service.
Second, Respondent argues that she was not able to respond to discovery until
November 7, 2025, because she was preparing for surgery “on or before”
September 8, 2025; she was incapacitated after the surgery; and her daughter
had a significant medical emergency “shortly thereafter.” However, the court’s
records reflect that from August 21, 2025, (the date discovery was served) to
September 25, 2025, (the date discovery responses were due), Respondent filed
six documents with the court, including a 126-page Objection. (ROAs 198-
203.) Based on the record before the court, clearly the Respondent had the
ability to at least request an extension of time to respond to discovery during
this time period.
Finally, in an untimely filed supplement to her opposition, Respondent argues
that imposing sanctions would be unjust because she is a person protected by
the Americans with Disabilities Act. Respondent claims that, due to various
physical and mental disabilities, she is unable to “complete complex legal tasks
within standard timeframes without accommodation.” (ROA 287, 2:8-12.) The
court finds such argument to be without legal merit as it is belied by
Respondent’s own evidence. In her initial Opposition, Respondent claims that
she first became aware of the discovery in October 2025 and that she completed
the responses thereto by October 29, 2025. (ROA 262, 4:12-14.) Thus,
Respondent was able to complete her responses to discovery within 30 days,
which is the time allotted by statute.
While Respondent produced evidence that she is on certain medications, there
is insufficient evidence for the court to find that her disabilities limit major life
activities so as to require a different ruling. Again, Respondent was able to file
six court documents during the time she was allegedly unable to respond to
discovery, and she was ultimately able to complete discovery responses within
30 days of her alleged receipt thereof.
No part of this order prohibits Respondent from otherwise seeking
accommodations through the court’s ADA Coordinator. The court only finds
that the information submitted in opposition to this motion is insufficient to
find that Respondent needed an accommodation to respond to the subject
discovery or that imposing sanctions against Respondent for necessitating this
discovery motion would be unjust.
For Respondent’s convenience, the information to contact the ADA
Coordinator is provided herein:
Orange County Superior Court
ADA Coordinator
700 Civic Center Drive West
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Telephone: (657) 622-7769
Email: adainformation@occourts.org
Pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure section 2030.290(c), the court awards
Petitioner attorney's fees in the amount of $1,060.00 payable by Respondent
Lorelei Ann Griggs.
Counsel for moving party is ordered to give notice of this ruling and may elect
to prepare, file and serve a proposed Order After Hearing.
